name: lead-quality-stands-out
about: LQ3c: an ordinary day whose lead-quality rows show many wrong numbers on one campaign and many missed hard requirements on the other — the part the office most needs.

output.headline: November 3, 2026: 2 campaigns spent $284.25, pulled 14,600 impressions, 203 clicks, and 7 leads at a $40.61 cost per lead.
points: Regional Class A — Joliet drove 6 of the day's 7 leads at $30.75 each across 9,120 impressions and a 1.5% click rate. Dedicated night runs returned 1 lead at $99.75 cost per lead on 5,480 impressions and a 1.1% click rate.
November 2026 has 28 days left; Meta is the only platform with recorded spend so far, at $612.30 for the month.

Lead quality over the last 14 days: Regional Class A — Joliet had 46.7% wrong numbers of those called — nearly half — which is worth a close look. It also had 3 leads who missed a hard requirement, making up 12.5% of its leads. Median time to first call was 11 minutes.

Lead quality for Dedicated night runs over the same 14 days is a sharper concern: 55.6% of its leads missed a hard requirement. Wrong numbers were 12.5% of those called, and median time to first call was 42 minutes.

The 2026-09-28 mature cohort shows 50.0% of leads converted to applicants, 12.5% hired, and 22.5% lost after conversion. The 2026-09-21 cohort sits at 44.7% converted, 10.5% hired, and 21.1% lost after conversion.
The 2026-10-26 cohort has 12 leads — 9 contacted, 3 converted, 1 applied, and 1 lost after conversion — but it is too young to judge rates yet.
